vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: virtuoso-skill
Version: 1.0.3

The virtuoso-skill bundle is a legitimate development aid for Cadence Virtuoso Skill programming, providing API lookup, code linting, and recommendation features. It includes a Flask-based web interface for interactive queries and utility scripts for processing API documentation. While some utility scripts (scripts/extract_functions.py and scripts/parse_api_data.py) contain environment-specific hardcoded paths for database generation, the core functionality is well-documented, lacks high-risk behaviors like data exfiltration or unauthorized command execution, and is entirely consistent with its stated purpose.

llm.summary: The skill's files and instructions mostly match a SKILL-language helper (chatbot + linter + API DB), but there are a few inconsistencies and small red flags (hidden unicode-control chars in SKILL.md, hard-coded local input path, a large compressed DB mismatch) that warrant caution before running it.

dimensions.detail: Name, description, and provided code (API database, chatbot, linter, parsers) are consistent with a Cadence Virtuoso SKILL-language developer helper. There are no unrelated environment variables or external service credentials requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md only instructs running the provided tools (chatbot, web UI, linter). Those tools legitimately read local API DB files and user SKILL source files. However: (1) two scripts (extract_functions.py and parse_api_data.py) include a hard-coded absolute input path (/root/.openclaw/qqbot/downloads/...) which would attempt to read a file from that location if executed; (2) the chatbot can start a Flask web server that will bind a local port (network exposure risk if run on a networked host). Neither is necessarily malicious, but both expand the runtime scope beyond simple read-only lookups and should be considered before execution.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec, no remote downloads, and no package manager pulls. It's instruction-only with bundled scripts and data files — lower install risk. The repository includes a large compressed DB file (references/skill_api_database_full.gz.json) which will be read by tools; nothing is downloaded at runtime in the provided code.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables, credentials, or config paths. The code only reads local files (API DB and user-specified SKILL files), which is proportionate for a linter and API reference tool.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill does not request persistent/system privileges. The code does not modify other skills or system-wide configurations. Running the chatbot/web server will open a local port but does not make permanent system changes.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package appears to be a coherent SKILL-language helper (chatbot, API DB, linter), but take the following precautions before running it: 1) Inspect SKILL.md and remove/visualize any hidden unicode control characters (prompt-injection risk). 2) Review scripts for hard-coded paths (extract_functions.py and parse_api_data.py reference /root/.openclaw/...), and avoid running them unless you know what files they will access. 3) Run the tools in an isolated environment (container or VM) first — the linter will read your codebase, and the chatbot's --web mode starts a Flask server that will bind a port. 4) Verify which API database file will be used: there is a small JSON (312 functions) and a very large compressed file; ensure you're comfortable with the contents before allowing the linter to load it. 5) If you lack trust in the origin (source is 'unknown'), prefer manual inspection and limited execution (e.g., run search/read-only functions) rather than running parsing/extraction scripts with elevated privileges. If you want, I can highlight the exact lines with hard-coded paths and show how to sanitize/remove hidden unicode characters.
llm.findings: [unicode-control-chars] unexpected: Scanner detected unicode control characters in SKILL.md. This may be an attempt to influence model or evaluation behavior via hidden characters; not necessary for a developer helper and should be removed/inspected.
